article_details.topic: How Disney+ Hotstar Managed 5 Cr+ Live Viewers During India's T20 World Cup Win (2024)
dates_referenced: Historical Reference Date: 18 Nov, 2023 (World Cup Semifinal: India vs New Zealand)

viewership_milestones.record_concurrency: 5 Crore+ (50 Million+) viewers during India's T20 World Cup 2024 win

past_records.india_vs_new_zealand_semifinal_nov_15_20: 5 Crore+ concurrent viewers globally at Wankhede Stadium match

viewership_milestones.industry_context: Many competitor OTT streaming platforms crash when traffic hits around 3 Crore viewers, but Hotstar maintained high availability without downtime.

backend_infrastructure_and_hardware_scal.traffic_handling_model: 100% of user traffic is handled by AWS EC2 compute instances and AWS S3 object storage
backend_infrastructure_and_hardware_scal.compute_capacity: 500+ AWS CPU instances from the C4 family
backend_infrastructure_and_hardware_scal.target_cpu_utilization: 75% average utilization to ensure safe buffer capacity for sudden spikes

instance_mix_strategy.definition: A balanced combination of different EC2 purchasing options to maintain performance and lower costs
instance_mix_strategy.on_demand_instances: Used for predictable, baseline workloads that need continuous, non-interruptible availability
instance_mix_strategy.spot_instances: Cost-effective option where Hotstar bids on spare AWS capacity for interruptible tasks to save significant money
instance_mix_strategy.smart_cost_management: Uses Machine Learning and data analytics on historical patterns to dynamically allocate instances and reduce hosting bills

reasons_for_selection: Handles concurrent data streams easily and fast
Easy and readable for developers to write and maintain
Makes finding and resolving application bugs straightforward

microservices_architecture.description: App is split into small, decoupled, independent services instead of a single monolith
microservices_architecture.role: Each microservice handles a dedicated business task, connects via clean APIs, and scales independently when traffic peaks

load_balancing.function: Evenly spreads millions of user requests across EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses so no single host gets overloaded

key_roles: Consumes and routes massive streams of live user data between systems with low latency
Horizontal scaling via distributed partitions across multiple servers
Data replication across nodes to protect against server crashes
Decouples services so a spike or bug in one service does not crash others

caching_layer.function: In-memory database that delivers sub-millisecond response times for rapid data access and real-time live match updates

database_and_storage.object_storage: Amazon S3 (stores huge media libraries, video chunks, and delivers streaming assets reliably)
database_scaling_strategies: Database sharding (splitting database across multiple nodes)

big_data_processing.function: Processes massive amounts of daily user behavior, engagement, and viewing analytics

cdn_and_video_delivery.global_cdn_partnerships: Multi-CDN network strategy that routes users to the nearest regional edge server and offers instant failover if one CDN drops

video_encoding_and_compression.adaptive_bitrate_streaming: Encodes video into multiple bitrates/quality levels, adjusting automatically to user internet speed to stop buffering
video_encoding_and_compression.bit_level_encoding: Optimizes video chunks to consume minimal bandwidth while preserving high video quality

why_hotstar_succeeded_where_others_crash.competitor_pitfall: Other streaming platforms use good tech (Node.js, Kafka, Kubernetes, Kibana, Jenkins), but fail because having cloud tools is not enough without an end-to-end scalable architecture design

multi_tiered_autoscaling.dynamic_resource_allocation: Scales every layer simultaneously (load balancers, microservices, databases, and CDNs) instead of just adding EC2 machines
multi_tiered_autoscaling.predictive_analytics: Machine learning models forecast spikes ahead of time using live match situations (falling wickets, overs remaining), user patterns, and social media buzz to scale before the surge hits

edge_computing.localized_processing: Processes viewer requests and caches video segments on edge servers close to the user, protecting core servers from traffic floods
edge_computing.real_time_edge_analytics: Detects and resolves local network congestion or edge server issues instantly before they reach central systems

data_pipeline_hygiene.fast_analytics_pipeline: Built rapid streaming pipelines so data processing delays never degrade live broadcast quality
data_pipeline_hygiene.bad_data_filtering: Automatically discards corrupted or bad events immediately so they do not skew autoscale metrics or business choices
data_pipeline_hygiene.accurate_metrics: Autoscaling depends on strictly validated metric triggers to prevent delayed responses to sudden user waves

android_client_tech_stack: Chuck Interceptor (in-app HTTP inspection and debugging)

article_overview.title: How Uber Finds Nearby Drivers at 1 Million Requests per Second?
article_overview.core_problem: Connecting millions of riders with the right nearby drivers instantly based on proximity, road traffic, and driver availability without system crashes.

why_efficient_matching_matters.rider_experience: Quick pickup and less waiting time lead to happy riders and higher app ratings.
why_efficient_matching_matters.driver_earnings: Less idle time between rides means drivers finish more rides per hour and maximize their total income.
why_efficient_matching_matters.platform_scalability: System can handle massive, sudden spikes in customer demand without slowing down or degrading performance.

core_technology_stack.real_time_location_tracking: Continuous GPS tracking from both rider and driver phones to keep current positions accurate.
core_technology_stack.geospatial_indexing: Breaks the world map into smaller regions using algorithms (like Quadtrees, Geohashes, or R-trees) so the system only searches local areas instead of scanning the whole database.
core_technology_stack.distributed_systems: Spreads data and requests across multiple independent servers so no single machine becomes a point of failure.
core_technology_stack.machine_learning: Analyzes historical trip data and live traffic conditions to forecast rider demand and optimize driver dispatches.

microservices_architecture.definition: Splitting the entire backend into smaller, independent services.
microservices_architecture.role: Separate services handle tasks like calculating fares, updating live driver locations, and processing ride requests in parallel.

geo_indexing_operations.mechanism: Organizes GPS coordinates into spatial bounding boxes.
geo_indexing_operations.advantage: Instead of full-table database searches, it instantly returns riders and available drivers within the exact same geographic boundary.

machine_learning_models.role: Predicts live supply-demand gaps using historical ride patterns, guidance inputs, and external event schedules.

dynamic_pricing_surge.role: Algorithms automatically increase ride fares when demand exceeds supply in a specific area, motivating more drivers to move there.

system_optimization_techniques.route_optimization: Considers road traffic, construction closures, and past trip data to suggest the quickest pickup and drop-off paths.
system_optimization_techniques.supply_demand_balancing: Maintains a healthy balance of available cars across regions to keep rider waiting times low.
system_optimization_techniques.request_batching: Groups multiple incoming ride requests together and processes them in batches, reducing computing load and boosting throughput.
system_optimization_techniques.dynamic_pricing_incentives: Balances driver distribution across zones during peak hours.

high_availability_and_reliability_strate.redundancy_and_replication: Duplicates critical backend components and data across multiple servers and data centers.
high_availability_and_reliability_strate.failover_mechanisms: Automatically reroutes incoming traffic away from failed nodes to healthy servers with minimal downtime.
high_availability_and_reliability_strate.distributed_architecture: Distributes services across multiple geographic regions to protect against local data center outages.
high_availability_and_reliability_strate.monitoring_and_alerting: Real-time health dashboards with automated alerts detect and flag issues instantly.
high_availability_and_reliability_strate.chaos_engineering: Intentionally creates simulated failures in the system to uncover hidden bugs before they cause real outages.
high_availability_and_reliability_strate.continuous_improvement: Ongoing code updates and architectural fixes to strengthen reliability.

handling_long_term_growth.hardware_upgrades: Regularly scales up server capacity and cloud infrastructure to handle rising request volumes.
handling_long_term_growth.algorithm_refinement: Constantly tweaks matching logic to make it faster, lighter, and more accurate.
handling_long_term_growth.data_driven_decisions: Uses continuous analytics to identify system bottlenecks and performance lags.
